authoritative_rust_surfaces.semantic: Canonical repository validation and lifecycle interpretation
authoritative_rust_surfaces.implementation: rust/crates/repopact-validation and the repopact-engine protocol dispatcher
authoritative_rust_surfaces.python_role: The direct validator entry point delegates to Rust. legacy_validate and validate_repo.validate remain an explicitly named comparator used by conformance tests, not a product fallback.

authoritative_rust_surfaces.semantic: Governed work-item creation, proposal and typed edits/transitions
authoritative_rust_surfaces.implementation: repopact-engine typed work operations backed by the Rust schema, validation, repository and analysis crates
authoritative_rust_surfaces.python_role: The CLI adapter preflights engine capabilities and validates the complete mutation response before reporting success.

authoritative_rust_surfaces.implementation: Rust repopact-graph and graph protocol handlers
authoritative_rust_surfaces.python_role: graph_cli transports typed requests and renders responses; it does not calculate graph results.
Product entry points use the Rust writer. generate_dashboard.write_dashboard remains a Python comparator/test utility and is used to create disposable conformance fixtures.

remaining_python_authoritative_surfaces.behavior: Python constructs and writes adopted/imported governance records; canonical Rust validation is checked afterward.
remaining_python_authoritative_surfaces.risk: These workflows still own record-authoring and migration semantics and can write before final Rust validation rejects the resulting repository.

remaining_python_authoritative_surfaces.behavior: Python applies repository repairs; canonical Rust validation is the final validity authority.
remaining_python_authoritative_surfaces.risk: Repair selection and mutation remain Python-owned.

remaining_python_authoritative_surfaces.behavior: Python decides and performs legacy-directory archival/retirement after canonical pre-validation, then asks Rust to validate the result.
remaining_python_authoritative_surfaces.risk: Retirement semantics and filesystem mutation remain Python-owned; post-validation cannot undo a completed retirement.

remaining_python_authoritative_surfaces.behavior: Python selects templates, allocates IDs and writes Markdown; Rust validates the repository and writes the derived dashboard.
These specialized or compatibility workflows retain Python policy/orchestration and file-write behavior, while applicable final repository validation/dashboard output uses Rust.
remaining_python_authoritative_surfaces.risk: They have not been proven to be thin adapters to a single Rust mutation authority.

results: Direct validator has no Python fallback; incompatible/malformed engine responses, inconsistent counts/diagnostics, missing required operations, unavailable engine preflight and conflicting mutation results fail closed.
Canonical Rust conformance: 37/37 cases passed; WI050 admission corpus: 8/8 vectors passed.
Complete Windows Python suite: 380 passed, 4 skipped.

architecture_conflict.source: Decision 0042, section describing the surface-by-surface authority boundary
architecture_conflict.recorded_boundary: init, adopt, import-plan, doctor, takeover, spec, generic decision/policy creation and check-frozen remain Python-authoritative or unmigrated unless WI056 independently proves a narrower migration.
architecture_conflict.conflict: RPS-007 requires Core alone to own governed mutation, while these accepted surfaces still make mutation or policy decisions in Python.
architecture_conflict.required_resolution: An operator-approved governance/API decision defining whether RPS-007 is narrowed to the already-migrated Rust surfaces or authorizing a separately scoped migration of the remaining Python-authoritative surfaces. No resolution is inferred here.

limitations: Published Workbench was inspected read-only; no Workbench parity or mutation-authority claim is made.
The full criterion is not satisfied because accepted Python-authoritative mutation surfaces remain.
